summary: Nigerian Pentecostal televangelist TB Joshua built a global following in Lagos on staged miracle videos while his church compound hid decades of rape, forced abortions, torture and a deadly 2014 building collapse.

evidence.note: Birth in 1963 in Ondo State, Nigeria
Church founded in 1986 and grows into a mass congregation
Miracle videos made for and shipped to British and South African evangelicals
Followers told to drop HIV drugs and chemotherapy; deaths in London
English disciple from Brighton joins hoping to be cured of being gay
LGBTQ children brought by parents for spiritual conversion
Sexual abuse of female disciples, isolation cells, forced abortions
Namibian victim taken at seventeen and confined for years
Pivot from TV to YouTube and Facebook after 2004 miracle broadcast ban
Fatal stampede over anointing water in Ghana
Anointing water sent to Sierra Leone during the 2014 Ebola outbreak
2014 collapse kills at least 116, mostly South African visitors; death in 2021

notes: Taxonomy examples list TB Joshua under organized-religion and religious-leader, so organized-religion is primary; the hosts repeatedly call SCOAN a cult, hence cults-new-religions secondary and org_type cult. The January 2024 BBC/openDemocracy exposé and his widow taking over are short codas, so reaches_present is false. Lagos is central (NG-LA).
